brief.deck: Zenity, the AI-agent security company founded in Tel Aviv and run commercially from New York, announced a $125M Series C led by Norwest on 3 August, with SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Hitachi Ventures and LG Technology Ventures joining. Total funding is about $185M; the valuation was not disclosed.
brief.the_case_p1: Qumra Capital joined the new investors; Vertex Ventures, Third Point Ventures, DTCP and Intel Capital returned. The $38M Series B, co-led by Third Point and DTCP with Microsoft's M12, closed in October 2024. In April Gartner named Zenity 'the company to beat' in AI agent governance. Founders Ben Kliger and Michael Bargury built security products together at Microsoft; the company now employs more than 230 people, about 150 in Israel, runs sales, marketing and operations from New York, and counts Fortune 500 and Global 2000 enterprises, SoftBank Corp among them, as customers.
brief.the_case_p2: Every AI agent an enterprise deploys, from Microsoft Copilot to custom builds, acts with someone's permissions; Zenity inventories them, limits what they can reach and detects when their intent drifts. The grid has bought defence in depth, CrowdStrike at Mercedes, Bitdefender at Ferrari, Keeper at Williams, Rubrik at McLaren, but nobody has bought the agent layer. The Norwest-led Series C funds exactly the global expansion a sponsorship serves.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Series C closed on 3 August with a global-expansion mandate, and Gartner's April verdict gives the brand a window to own its category before rivals catch up. The United States GP in Austin (late October) and Las Vegas (November) sit inside the horizon; teams settle 2027 rosters in the fourth quarter.
brief.why_team_para: Cadillac's debut roster has TWG AI as exclusive AI partner, Core Scientific for the data centre and IFS for enterprise software, and no cybersecurity partner, so the agent-security lane is clean. A team assembling its estate in 2026 is adopting agents inside Copilot and its own AI programme at the same moment, with no legacy controls to retrofit. Zenity's New York commercial base and Fortune 500 customer list match an American flag-bearer selling to enterprise CIOs.
brief.value_content: MODE A - operational. Zenity inventories every AI agent in the team's estate and what each can reach; enforces least privilege before an agent touches design, supplier or strategy data; and watches agent behaviour at runtime for prompt injection and intent drift. For a first-season team standing up Copilot beside an exclusive AI programme, it is the control layer that lets engineers use agents without exposing the car.
brief.deal_arch_para: Entry as Official AI Security Partner, in the cybersecurity category. <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9.5'>THREE YEARS</font>, 2027-2029, covering the expansion the Series C funds. Estimated $2-4M a year, part in platform licences. Scope: garage and car placement, an 'agents in the garage' content series, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality for CISOs and CIOs, a Cadillac reference deployment.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Kliger co-founded Zenity in 2021 with CTO Michael Bargury after leading security products together at Microsoft, is based in New York. Path: Bargury, and Keren Herscovici, VP Finance and Corporate Development. No chief marketing officer is listed; marketing is led at director level (reported).
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with Gartner and the empty agent lane.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Ben, Gartner says you are the company to beat, and no Formula 1 team has an AI-agent security partner. Cadillac is building its estate from zero this year. 25 minutes before Austin to see what that lane is worth?”
score_cells: Round announced 3 Aug; Austin and Las Vegas inside the window.

brief.bottom_line: A $125M Series C led by Norwest, with SoftBank, Hitachi and LG, Gartner's 'company to beat' verdict and an untouched agent-security lane at the American debutant put Zenity in a window to buy category ownership, with Austin and Las Vegas inside it. An undisclosed valuation, no marketing officer and Cadillac's price point hold the score at 72.

why_now.label: Trigger
why_now.text: Zenity announced a $125M Series C led by Norwest on 3 August 2026, with Qumra Capital, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Hitachi Ventures and LG Technology Ventures joining and Vertex, Third Point, DTCP and Intel Capital returning. The company release, Fortune and Calcalist carry the same figures; the valuation was not disclosed.

why_now.label: Analyst verdict
why_now.text: Gartner's 17 April 2026 report named Zenity 'the company to beat' in AI agent governance. A category leader has a short window to turn an analyst's verdict into market awareness before better-funded platforms crowd in; the Series C is explicitly for global expansion.

why_now.label: A company built for the enterprise buyer
why_now.text: More than 230 employees, sales, marketing and operations run from New York, and a customer base of Fortune 500 and Global 2000 enterprises, SoftBank Corp among them. The audience in a Formula 1 suite is the audience Zenity already sells to.

why_now.label: Calendar window
why_now.text: The United States GP in Austin (late October) and the Las Vegas GP (November) are the two US rounds left in 2026; teams close 2027 partner rosters in the fourth quarter. A deal agreed before Austin can be announced there and activated in full for 2027.

why_team.label: The open lane
why_team.text: Cadillac's debut roster carries TWG AI as exclusive AI partner, Core Scientific for the data centre, IFS for enterprise software, plus Claro, Jim Beam, Tenneco and Tommy Hilfiger. No cybersecurity partner, and no team on the grid has an AI-agent security partner: the category is Zenity's to name.

why_team.label: A greenfield estate adopting agents
why_team.text: A team assembling factories, suppliers and systems in 2026 is deploying AI agents inside Copilot-class tools and its own exclusive AI programme at the same moment, with no legacy controls to retrofit. That is the customer profile Zenity's platform was designed for.

why_team.label: An American commercial fit
why_team.text: Zenity runs sales, marketing and operations from New York and sells to Fortune 500 CIOs and CISOs. Cadillac is the GM-backed American flag-bearer with a commercial team hired to reach exactly that enterprise audience.

why_team.label: Why not the others
why_team.text: Every other cybersecurity lane on the grid is occupied, from CrowdStrike at Mercedes to Cato Networks at Alpine. Haas and Racing Bulls are open but lack the AI programme that makes agent security a live workstream rather than a logo.

value.label: Operational workstream (Mode A)
value.text: An inventory of every AI agent in the team's estate and what each can reach; least-privilege enforcement before an agent touches design, supplier or strategy data; runtime detection of prompt injection and intent drift. Engineers use agents freely, and the security lead can see what they did.

value.label: Commercial lift for the team
value.text: A partner selling to Fortune 500 security and IT leaders brings a guest list of CIOs and CISOs to Austin and Las Vegas, the audience Cadillac's B2B partners want in the suite.

value.label: Content and ecosystem
value.text: 'Agents in the garage': co-produced content on how a new Formula 1 team lets its engineers use AI safely, a Cadillac reference deployment for Zenity's enterprise sales, and a story that fits a debutant building everything from scratch.

value.label: What the team gives back
value.text: Official AI Security Partner designation in the cybersecurity category, garage and car placement, Austin and Las Vegas hospitality, driver and engineering access for Zenity's channels.
